instructions: Peel the onion and cut it in half. Leave one half in one piece and finely chop the other. Peel the 4 garlic cloves and leave them whole.

Set a large soup pot over medium high with nothing in it for about 2 minutes, until it's hot. Add the bay leaf, the 6 allspice berries, the cinnamon stick, the 2 cloves, the onion half in one piece and the garlic. Toast them for 4 to 5 minutes, moving them now and then, until they smell fragrant and the onion has dark spots.

Pour in the 6 cups chicken broth and bring it to a boil. Add the 1 lb chicken thighs and turn the heat down to medium low. Simmer gently for about 20 minutes. You're cooking them to 175°F in the thickest part, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when the juices run clear and there's no pink left.
Meanwhile, cut the 4 tortillas into strips about 1/4 inch wide.

Heat 6 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium high. Drop in one strip. When it bubbles fast, the oil is ready. Fry the strips in two batches for 1 to 2 minutes, turning them, until they're golden and crisp. Lift them onto a plate lined with paper towels and sprinkle with 1/4 tsp of the salt.
Seed and finely chop the red pepper. Core and chop the 2 tomatoes.
Seed the habanero, slice it very thin and put it in a small bowl for the table. Wash your hands well afterwards. It's very hot.
Lift the chicken onto a cutting board. Pour the broth through a sieve into a large bowl and throw away the spices, onion and garlic. Wipe out the pot.
Heat the last 2 tbsp oil in the pot over medium. Add the chopped onion and the red pepper and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 6 to 7 minutes more, stirring, until they break down and the mix smells sweet.
Meanwhile, shred the chicken with two forks.
Pour the broth back into the pot and add the chicken and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Simmer for 10 minutes.
While it simmers, juice 2 of the limes, about 1/4 cup, and cut the third into thin rounds. Chop a handful of the cilantro and dice the avocado.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the lime juice. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Ladle it into bowls and top each one with the tortilla strips, cilantro, avocado and a lime round.
Serve hot, with the sliced habanero on the side.
method_notes: All three read versions poach chicken in broth, cook a sofrito of onion, sweet pepper and tomato separately, add both back with plenty of lime juice and top the bowls with fried tortilla strips and cilantro. Nourished Kitchen, the lead, dry toasts bay, allspice, cinnamon and cloves with onion and garlic before the broth goes in, strains them out, fries the sofrito in lard and serves sliced habanero and avocado at the table. Caroline's Cooking poaches the chicken with oregano and bay and uses a mild wax pepper, and Running to the Kitchen starts from a homemade carcass stock. This one follows the lead with chicken thighs, oil in place of lard and regular limes, since Yucatecan limas are hard to find. No version had 20 or more ratings and RecipeTin Eats (the trusted cook for Mexican) has no version, so the first read version leads.
